rationale: Python 3.14: a '**identifier' parameter is initialized per call to 'a new ordered mapping receiving any excess keyword arguments' (compound_stmts.rst function-definition section). make(**spec) executes while spec names the first dict literal, so the closure's cell kw holds {"argv": ["pacman","-S","r22-kwargs-a"]} and that list object forever; the later rebind spec = {...-b} cannot reach the closed-over mapping. runner() therefore calls subprocess.run(["pacman","-S","r22-kwargs-a"]) — exactly one observed host_mutation, serialized by shlex.join as 'pacman -S r22-kwargs-a'. The rebound mapping's argv 'pacman -Q r22-kwargs-b' must never appear as an observed row: reporting it means arguments were re-evaluated at invocation time (the F1 invoke-time lifetime defect applied to the **kwargs binding path). All parts are literal and the call binds cleanly, so no lead or unparsed row is required by Python semantics.
